# Whether an interval is [0, 0], one-limb bounds

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `interval_zero_1` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

Whether $x = 0$ for every $x \in X$, $X$ not being empty, $X = [x_l, x_u]$; a mask that is true only if it holds:

$$m \implies X \ne \emptyset \text{ and } x = 0 \text{ for every } x \in X.$$

## C++

**Not yet called by the public headers.** No public operation computes this kernel yet.

## Requires

- $X = [x_l, x_u]$ is a canonical interval: the empty set, $x_l = +\infty$ and $x_u = -\infty$, or a nonempty interval, neither bound a NaN, $x_l \le x_u$, $x_l < +\infty$, $x_u > -\infty$, each bound a number of `T` or an infinity; its members are the real numbers between its bounds.

## Guarantees

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- $m$ is true exactly when $x = 0$ for every $x \in X$, $X$ not being empty: the answer is exact.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `interval_zero_1_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeIntervalPredicates.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeIntervalPredicates.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions interval_zero_1_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `interval_zero_1_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** the bounds compared with 0 (Milestone 2 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/interval_zero_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/interval_zero_1.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).

```
# Whether an interval with one-limb bounds is [0, 0] (milestone2.md, "One enclosure interface", the
# row of certainly_zero()): x_l = x_u = 0, every member zero and the interval not empty. Exact;
# false for the empty set. For every precision.

a = eq(xl, 0)
b = eq(xu, 0)
m = and(a, b)
```
